items.q: What should you remember about **Fun → production in weeks**?
items.a: **community-note denial → internal dogfood** → public rewrite blog; AI collapses "language choice is one-way" assumption.

items.q: What should you remember about **Memory bug class as rewrite driver**?
items.a: **Bun 1.3.14 sample dominated** by UAF/OOB/leaks/double-free/races; Jared attributes unusual GC+manual mix, not Zig itself.

items.q: What should you remember about **compiler enforcement vs style guides**?
items.a: **style guides + review/linters are best-effort social contracts;** Rust makes the contract a compile error (~20% of Bun was already C++ with same enforcement problem).

items.q: What should you remember about **$165K vs engineer-years**?
items.a: **Netflix rewrite comparator**: million-dollar fully-loaded cost + freeze; 11-day AI port + months of cleanup still wins the cost/quality/speed triangle.

items.q: What should you remember about **fresh context agent review**?
items.a: **after each task, spawn separate no-context agents on** the changeset ("did it do the thing? bugs?") then apply feedback; Primeagen's favorite AI use for ~8 months.

items.q: What should you remember about **Parallel error/test shards**?
items.a: **many Claude Code workers in git worktrees; one** error or test slice per agent; loop until 16K errors and then all unit tests pass.

items.q: What should you remember about **Mechanical translation ≠ idiomatic**?
items.a: **structure may mirror Zig;** lifetimes/style guides were front-loaded; expect heavy post-port cleanup ("refactorbation").

items.q: What should you remember about **Verification gate**?
items.a: **compile-green ≠ ship; linker panic on** bun --version; unit-test fleet was the confidence signal for "this might actually work".

items.q: What should you remember about **Devtools love**?
items.a: **Primeagen values the orchestration pattern (change → dual** review → fix → shard) more than tribal Zig/Rust takes; built Prime Agent Review into Neovim/cloud-agent workflow.
